landed: process_ledger/writer.rs: PostgresProcessLedgerStore -> SurrealProcessLedgerStore over the kernel_process_lifecycle table. The two ON CONFLICT update lists were reproduced field-for-field in Rust: START coalesces optional identity columns and takes the earliest started_at but never touches stopped_at/exit_code/stop_reason, so a replayed START cannot erase a STOP that already landed; STOP overwrites only the stop triple. Both merges stay idempotent, so the existing retain-and-retry loop re-converges.

session_checkpoint/writer.rs: append-only writes keyed on checkpoint_id. An existing id is skipped and NOT counted in the returned row count, reproducing ON CONFLICT (checkpoint_id) DO NOTHING plus rows_affected, so an idempotent retry neither errors nor double-counts.

flight_recorder/fr_emitter.rs: batch flusher appends kernel_event_ledger through the embedded store. Ledger ordering stays owned by the database via event_sequence DEFAULT sequence::nextval. A real regression was prevented: the old batch was one transaction, so a mid-batch failure rolled back and the retained batch replayed each event exactly once; with per-record commits the flusher now drains the successfully-written prefix before propagating the error, restoring exactly-once.
process_ledger/table.rs: deleted the three PostgreSQL DDL/DML constants as dead residue.
progress_2026_08_16.known_regression_disclosed: Batch atomicity is lost in the process ledger: rows now commit individually rather than as one transaction. The merges are idempotent so recovery still converges, but this is a real semantic change and is recorded rather than hidden.
progress_2026_08_16.deliberate_non_regression: process_ledger/reclaim.rs went 4 -> 5 errors ON PURPOSE. Its store no longer has a PgPool, and reclaim depends on an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE stopped_at IS NULL ... RETURNING whose lock covers the kill-and-STOP decision. Emulating that with read-then-write would be a silent correctness regression, so the honest compile error was left in place.

findings.failure_scenario: Two recovery owners claim the same abandoned process at the same timestamp. Owner A's stale exact STOP is rejected by SurrealDB, but the typed process-ledger layer erases the contract-specific conflict classification. Callers cannot distinguish stale ownership from generic storage failure, and the mandatory negative-path proof aborts before verifying that owner B's durable sentinel remains intact and can finalize exactly once.
required_product_changes: In SurrealProcessLedgerStore::write_batch_inner, preserve and classify the HSK-PROCESS-LEDGER-RECLAIM-CONFLICT result before generic StorageError-to-ProcessLedgerError conversion.

Return a deterministic typed ProcessLedgerError whose display contract includes `exact reclaim STOP did not own the current durable sentinel`; do not weaken the test and do not convert the conflict to success.
Prefer a structured query outcome/error classification over brittle free-text parsing if the Surreal adapter exposes one; keep the transaction rollback boundary unchanged.

Retain the equal-timestamp/distinct-owner adversarial case and prove after the stale failure that the row is still owned by owner B, owner B can finalize it, and close/reopen shows exactly one terminal result with unchanged chronology/metadata.

After the source change, rerun the full nine-test process_ledger::writer::surreal_restart_tests target, then crash_recovery_e2e with app-runtime,surreal-test-support,test-utils, because both consume the changed writer semantics.
